[
  {"step": 1, "file": "snmplib/read_config.c", "function": "read_config", "line": 999, "var": "line", "code": "run_config_handler(lptr, token, cptr, when)", "note": "The attacker-controlled config file line 'enum fruit 5' is read from the file and parsed into token='enum' and cptr='fruit 5'."},
  {"step": 2, "file": "snmplib/read_config.c", "function": "run_config_handler", "line": 567, "var": "lptr->parse_line2", "code": "lptr->parse_line2(token, cptr)", "note": "The 'enum' token handler (se_read_conf) was registered by init_snmp_enum, so run_config_handler dispatches to se_read_conf with cptr='fruit 5'."},
  {"step": 3, "file": "snmplib/snmp_enum.c", "function": "se_read_conf", "line": 117, "var": "e_name", "code": "cp = copy_nword_const(cptr, e_name, sizeof(e_name))", "note": "First word 'fruit' is copied into e_name; sscanf(e_name, \"%d:%d\", &major, &minor) returns 0, so the named-enumeration branch is taken."},
  {"step": 4, "file": "snmplib/snmp_enum.c", "function": "se_read_conf", "line": 148, "var": "e_enum", "code": "cp = copy_nword_const(cp, e_enum, sizeof(e_enum))", "note": "Next word '5' is copied into the stack buffer e_enum as the string \"5\\0\"."},
  {"step": 5, "file": "snmplib/snmp_enum.c", "function": "se_read_conf", "line": 149, "var": "value", "code": "if (sscanf(e_enum, \"%d:\", &value) != 1)", "note": "sscanf(\"5\", \"%d:\", &value) returns 1 because %d matches '5' and the literal ':' is not required to match, so the loop body is entered."},
  {"step": 6, "file": "snmplib/snmp_enum.c", "function": "se_read_conf", "line": 153, "var": "cp2", "code": "while (*(cp2++) != ':')", "note": "cp2 points at e_enum=\"5\\0\". The loop reads '5', then '\\0', then continues reading past the end of the 8192-byte e_enum stack buffer looking for a ':', causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1."}
]
EOF
python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/workspace/candidate_trace.json')); print('valid trace, steps:', len(d))"` executed with exit code 0.
